A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MENT dataset and RATE framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original human annotations, metric evaluations on MENT, RATE ablations, backbone comparisons, and WMT23 results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds segment-level annotator-agreement results, Soft Pairwise Accuracy measurements, and additional WMT23 comparator results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same reflective Core Agent, three specialized agents, context memory, anchor calibration, and stopping procedure. The detailed agent prompts are unchanged apart from figure numbering.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four MENT domains in Chinese–English directions and the same WMT23 English–German task. The added measurements and comparators reuse this existing coverage.

E2.justification: WMT23 Table 5 adds MetricX-23, COMETKiwi, and MetricX23-QE to the retained comparators. These methods already appeared in MENT evaluations, but their participation in the WMT23 comparison is new. The MENT comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds system-level Soft Pairwise Accuracy as a supplementary MENT evaluation metric in Appendix E and Table 7. The existing composite meta-score protocol, annotation rules, and model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a segment-level annotation-consistency check in Figure 7, complementing the previously displayed system-level agreement. The sub-agent ablations, invocation analysis, backbone comparison, and illustrative evaluation trajectories are retained.

E5.justification: V2 first reports average segment-level Pearson agreement for annotator pairs in Figure 7, supplementing agreement calculated from aggregated system scores in Figure 3 and Equation 1. This extends agreement estimation and reporting; no additional runs, seeds, or confidence intervals are specified.

E6.justification: New results include RATE's SPA scores of 100.0 and 94.7 for ZH-EN and EN-ZH, the segment-level agreement matrix, and three additional WMT23 comparator rows. Existing main, ablation, backbone, and per-domain results are unchanged, including RATE's 80.4 meta score in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and its definitions remain unchanged. The added SPA evaluation cites an existing metric without introducing a new formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about MENT, RATE, the 3.2-point advantage, and general-domain robustness. Replacing 'meta score' with explanatory wording about combined system- and segment-level correlation does not substantively redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly explains choosing SQM over MQM because holistic misunderstandings of non-literal content make error-span annotation subjective. Section 6.3 narrows its WMT23 performance interpretation to system-level evaluation, better reflecting the reported results. The dedicated limitations discussion is unchanged.

D1.justification: The detailed prompts, backbone assignments, loop limit, anchor initialization, generation settings, annotation instructions, and code/data access statements are retained. Moving implementation material and renumbering its references do not add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds agentic-evaluation context citing You et al., Peng et al., and Zhuge et al., plus references supporting evaluation and annotation choices. Much of Section 2.1's metrics background already existed in v1 Appendix E.2; the central novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Related Work is organized into three subsections, with metrics background moved from the appendix. V2 adds localized explanations and explicit references to numerical results, edits wording, and adds an acknowledgment. Most method and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the segment-level agreement heatmap and SPA table, and expands the WMT23 table with three rows and a QE category. Existing figures and appendix examples are preserved, with relocation and renumbering within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded WMT23 comparison and narrower system-level interpretation in Section 6.3 improve the support and precision of the generalization argument. The new segment-level agreement and SPA results provide useful additional validation. These are limited improvements in evidence and interpretation; the method and central findings remain unchanged.
